instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Nine starts after a January arrival, still adjusting to the speed of the league; the defender he became arrives the following August, and the jump to 88 is a real change rather than drift.
Half of the best defence in Europe, in a side that conceded 22 and won the European Cup.
PFA Player of the Year and fourteen consecutive clean sheets; the best season by a centre-half in the league since Ferdinand the year before.
Captain of the champions and thirty-five starts; back to something close to his 2008/09 level.
Fifteen starts before the move to Celtic in December; no drop in level, just half a season.
A World Cup winner months earlier and among the best defenders in the world; a shade below his Milan peak but still elite, above Adams (88) in 1998/99.
Thirty-four, fifteen starts, and losing the shirt to John Terry; the pace and the recovery were finally gone.
Thirty-six starts and Chelsea’s player of the year in a side that took a Champions League place on the last day; for two seasons among the best three or four keepers in the division.
Banned from late January after Selhurst Park. Rated on the football played, not the games missed.
Captain and champion again but visibly declining; retired at the end of the season aged 30.
Ever-present in the side that finished second with 86 points; twelve goals from wide right and the hardest running in the league.
Three starts at 30 after Derby’s relegation; effectively out of the top flight.
Four years on from the 1997/98 row: a raw teenager at Palace then, a functioning Premier League centre-forward by 23.
The season Ferguson picked him against every good midfield in Europe; energy, positional sense and use of the ball all at their peak.
An ever-present in the fifteen-point Sunderland side, which is evidence about the side rather than about him.
Five starts at 34; below the standard by then.
Chronic back and shin problems; effectively his last season of regular football, at 25.
Eight league goals from centre-half, nearly all headers, in an Everton side that finished fifth; the England call-up that followed was deserved.
Seventeen starts and an unhappy first season after the move; the player was the same, the settled place in a back four was not.
Twenty-one years old, captain of a side that reached an FA Cup final, and five goals from central midfield.
Three starts at 39 as emergency third-choice cover; rated as the player he was at that point, not the Leeds keeper of 1992.
Fourteen goals and genuinely frightening in a straight line; the finishing never caught up with the pace.
Nine starts after the Leeds move; could not get in the side.
Thirty-six starts for a relegated Norwich; still frightening in a straight line, still an unreliable finisher.
Germany’s first choice and an ever-present in an unbeaten side; elite, a rung below the very best keepers.
Ten clean sheets across a Champions League run at thirty-five; his best Arsenal season after the first.
Lost the shirt to Almunia and did not get it back.
PFA Team of the Year after a broken leg cost him most of 1995/96; eight assists from left-back and the best left-foot delivery in the division that season.
Two divisions and two seasons on from Liverpool; at 31 a steady, well-delivered left-back for a newly promoted side rather than the PFA pick of 1996/97.
Thirty-three and the best player in a mid-table Spurs side; the late runs and the finishing were intact, the legs less so.
A difficult first English season, played wide before the move into central midfield settled him.
Eleven assists and an England cap; elite delivery, nothing else above the standard.
Two seasons outside the top flight in between; at 34 a squad left-sided player whose delivery was still the only part of his game above the level.
An ever-present in the back four that kept Stoke up on their return; overwhelming in both boxes and comfortable with nothing else asked of him.
Two lost seasons at Leeds and abroad in between; at 28 a fringe player for a promoted side, not the England winger of 1994.
Six starts for a Bradford side relegated with 26 points; at 29 he was finished as a top-flight footballer.
Six years of Rangers, PSV and knee trouble between this and the Everton rows; he came back a lesser player.
Eleven assists from wide after two seasons out of the side; Wimbledon’s set-piece taker.
Ever-present captain of a promoted Portsmouth side that stayed up; a better defender at 33 than he had been at Barnsley six years earlier.
Nineteen; a big, athletic keeper with obvious raw material who went on to play for England.
Arguably the best goalkeeper outside the top four in this season; shot-stopping close to elite, sits with Flowers (81) rather than Seaman (86).
Half a season of the best form of his career before a January move to Real Madrid; aggressive, a better passer than the caricature, and Everton’s driving force in a fourth-placed side.
The same season and the same footballer as the Everton row; the move did not change him.
